newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DILEMMA FOR UNITED AS JUVENTUS CLASH LOOMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DILEMMA FOR UNITED AS JUVENTUS CLASH LOOMS.

text.p: Injuries have presented Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson with a tactical dilemma as he prepares his side to face Juventus next Wednesday.

Defender Phil Neville and hard-tackling midfielder Roy Keane are both ruled out of the Champions' League match in Turin, and Ferguson takes his team to Leeds for a premier league clash on Saturday knowing he cannot afford another injury blow to his defence.
"I'm not going to say that we're down to the bare bones, because that would be unfair," the Scotsman said after United's disappointing 1-1 draw with newly-promoted Derby on Wednesday.
"But the fact that we haven't got Phil or Roy does make it a concern that we don't get any more defenders injured at Leeds, that's for sure."

Ferguson dropped his habitual 4-4-2 formation at Derby, deploying Norwegian Ronny Johnsen alongside David May and Gary Pallister in a three-man defence, with Gary Neville and Denis Irwin playing as wingbacks.
But United looked far from comfortable with the system as they slipped to their third consecutive draw, and Ferguson now has to decide which formation to use against the Italians.
"In some ways it was okay at Derby, and I didn't think there were any problems with the centrebacks," Ferguson said.
"It was in the other positions that the problems came. The wider players need to have the confidence to stay forward and not worry about what's happening behind them."
"We can play a lot of systems with the players we've got, and should be capable of winning with any of them," he said. "At Derby we allowed them to advance into our half far too often."
Better news for Ferguson was UEFA's decision this week to waive the suspension that threatened to keep Frenchman Eric Cantona out of the showdown with the European champions.

Soccer's European governing body decided Cantona served his one-match suspension last season, when he missed out on United's UEFA Cup campaign because of an earlier eight-month ban imposed on him for attacking a fan.
"Eric's delighted, and it's a good boost for us," Ferguson said. "In a game of that nature (against Juventus) you want all your best players."
